saints.name: St. Josephine Bakhita
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Sudanese girl seized into slavery who found her true freedom in Christ and became a beloved Canossian sister in Italy…
biography: Born in Darfur in the Sudan about 1869, she was kidnapped as a child by slave-traders — who mockingly named her Bakhita, “the fortunate” — and endured years of cruelty under a succession of masters. Brought to Italy, she came to know the Christian faith through the Canossian sisters at Venice, was baptized Josephine, and, a court having declared her free, entered the Canossian Daughters of Charity.

For some fifty years she served her community at Schio with humility and gentleness, remembered for her constant trust in the will of “the Master,” her name for God. She died in 1947 and was canonized in 2000 by Pope John Paul II.
saints.knownFor: Her witness of forgiveness and faith after a childhood in slavery.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Josephine Bakhita (vatican.va)
